Phyra walked through the Primrose. A thing he was looking for, a thing he would find. The gods had become weak and no longer held large power over the mortals. A weapon to destroy the Oroborii, a weapon he would find in his need. Upon a glade he stumbled, suffused with moonlight and had a heady, chilling throb in the air. A throb that made your veins want to rip themselves out from under your skin and dance an ancient rite lost to time, a throb that made your face want to peel off and find a new owner. It was an eldritch power, a lost reflection of a sleeping god outside of time. Linger too long, and you would find yourself muttering phrases that made your bones grind and your hairs tie into other-dimensional knots.

In the glade, there was a monolith. A pillar of obsidian that had a perfectly square base, yet when you counted it the faces never quite added up to four. In on itself and out of itself it folded, making the top seem like it stretched into the sky. As the god of order approached it, his foot hit something which shifted a few feet into the darkness. The cold, cold darkness. Where the rats lurked, the rats in the walls. He rummaged around in the leaf cover, and came up with a skull. A skull of a thing that should not have a skull, a skull with a naturally bisected jaw and conical eye sockets. Dropping it, he shuddered. This was the place of things that should not be, things that should have been forgotten by time but instead chose to lurk in the corner of your eye, just past your peripheral vision - blink, and it flits away. You think it's gone, but it hides in the back of your mind - pushing you to do the things that no sane person would ever do. They pushed you to come out to glades like this in the night, when the moon was full and the throb of the otherwhere threaded into your grey matter through your nostrils and ears, and build a cairn. A simple pile of rocks - at first it would be only you, but others would come. Cloaked in red, all adding a stone to the cairn and receding back into the foreground. Someone would produce a flute from somewhere on their person, and to the piping of the demonic flute they would dance, and the line between man and beast would blur. Extra arms where there were once none, inverted noses, sometimes becoming something else altogether. Eventually the piper would too fall to the madness, and the spell would fade. Figures vanishing, the red men would fold back into the shadows, back into their normal lives like you once were, but they too would have the little figure in the corner of their eyes. Telling them, *come to the glade*.

And they would obey.

Phyra came closer and closer. Quick eyes caught the mark of a god long forgotten by the races of the world. A lidless eye, the pupil a double helix collapsing in on itself. The mark of Tymoro. Once the god of luck and chance, he had become corrupted by time - god of the dice and cards no more, now the Watcher God, patron of the eldritch and that which should not be. God of instability. God of madness. Chaos in the finest of ways. Worshippers perpetuated by an endless memetic fugue, recursing upon itself until the seeds of madness had been sown across the entirety of existence. It was an evil place, where an evil thing lived. A guardian of the Primrose from days lost to time - the Guardian of Probability. It had taken on the essence of its creator over the aeons, becoming steadily more unstable. Phyra put his hand on the obelisk. The throb was becoming unbearable now, and he could hear the voices, oh the voices, gibbering and jabbering in tongues unheard of.

His will he pushed towards it, and *it pushed back*. The voices now formed a harsh discord with the shrieking of a flute, drilling into the very essence of the god. Again, he pushed and found… *bemusal*. The Guardian had found his request interesting, a new opportunity to spread the memetic plague. Phyra took this to mean acceptance, and the presence mostly vanished from the obelisk. In the corner of his vision, Phyra noticed something. He blinked, and it went away.

Above the ruins of the Tree of Life, the air collapsed and folded in on itself. The throb began, slowly at first but growing exponentially. A fault in reality itself formed, and from the void came eight orbs. One might call them black, but that would be improper. Black is the absence of light. They were the absence of order. Underneath it, the Oroborous lazed. A dumb creature, fat and lazy - ripe for the coming harvest. It descended down upon the Oroborous, and the orbs began orbiting in upon eachother in a way that defied proper explanation. The heads of the beast struck at it, but they simply vaporized upon coming near to it - massive instability introduced into atomic bonds *en massé*. With each one vaporizing came a miniature sun, flaring then winking out of existence like holes being poked in the tar-like night sky. Closer it came to the Oroborous, and as it approached the very essence of the beast began to burn away into the æther. The heads fell like rain, shrunken and withered husks drifting like so many leaves upon the wind as they simply dried up and snapped off with a blood-curdling crack, like a child popping the head off of a dandelion. As the last head fell, it blackened and compressed, falling into the ground in the form of a black obelisk inscribed with the Lidless Eye. It stabbed itself into the ground, and where it fell a forest grew, gnarled and yet freshly matured. Without the bulk of the Oroborous supporting it, the skeleton of the Tree of Life collapsed in upon itself and disintegrated. The Guardian winked out of sight.

At the Great Roost, another Oroborous terrorized the Schrykes. This time, the Guardian manifested as a humanoid. Two arms, two legs, one head. He stomped his foot, and where his heel contacted the ground a crack formed. It raced along the ground tracing the outline of the Oroborous there, and then the ground fell. Not into the Underground, but into the Void. Down the Oroborous fell into infinite darkness, dragged down by the seething maw of the inky black and all its tentacles. The hole expanded, swallowing up a large portion of the Great Roost and all that resided there. Schrykes attempting to fly away were met with an irresistible force pulling them into the void - it swallowed them and then they were gone. For a short while this persisted, before the rift vanished and all that was left was the footprint of the great portal to the Void. The Guardian walked atop this barren area for a bit, then vanished. The Schryke Empress would find in her possession within the night a small cubic onyx crystal inscribed with the sign of the Lidless Eye.

Above the husk of Arsenal the Guardian hung. Taking this time the form of a singular floating dodecahedron, it mused upon the scene below. The Oroborous had eaten most of the once proud citadel that had stood impervious to all - now all that remained was a small portion of the mountain, formed into a overhand. The demons swarmed the area like a flood of black tar. *A fitting punishment is in order* it mused. It span, faster and faster, then stopped. A ray of dark flitted down to the beast. Where it touched, a tiny bit of the beast became stone. The patch began to spread at a faster and faster rate, quickly engulfing the entire beast. The heads and necks snapped at the joints and fell down the new mountain, forming rubble at the base. A different fate befell the demons, they simply turned into pillars of salt and blew away on the wind. In the Oroborous's place stood a mountain, similar to the one it had devoured but not quite - the average person would not take notice. Around it, the land was scorched and barren, and if one looked at the rubble in a certain way, they could pick out a symbol. The Lidless Eye. The Guardian chuckled softly to itself, and vanished back into the Primrose.
